messages:
maria_garcia: Hey folks — prepping a small TF change to annotate a serviceAccount in the analytics namespace for IRSA. Quick sanity check before I apply?

maria_garcia: here's the k8s resource I'm adding in terraform: ```hcl
resource \"kubernetes_service_account\" \"analytics_sa\" {
  metadata {
    name = \"analytics-sa\"
    namespace = \"analytics\"
    annotations = {
      \"eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn\" = \"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-analytics-IRSA\"
    }
  }
}
```

tom_s: generally looks fine. two quick checks: 1) does the IAM role trust policy reference the cluster OIDC provider? 2) are any existing pods relying on the old node-iam mapping (kube2iam/kiam)?

maria_garcia: role exists and already used by a batch job. trust policy snippet: ```json
{
  \"Version\": \"2012-10-17\",
  \"Statement\": [{
    \"Effect\": \"Allow\",
    \"Principal\": {
      \"Federated\": \"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:oidc-provider/oidc.eks.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/id/ABCDEF\"
    },
    \"Action\": \"sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity\"
  }]
}
```

devops-eli: sounds ok. reminder: the OIDC provider must exactly match the cluster OIDC thumbprint/issuer in AWS. Also if you created the role manually, confirm the condition on \"StringEquals\" for sub/namespace/name if you want narrow scope vs broad.

maria_garcia: I'm scoping by namespace/name: \"system:serviceaccount:analytics:analytics-sa\" in the trust condition.

infra-bot: terraform plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy. Planned: kubernetes_service_account.analytics_sa +1

sre-anna: couple of operational notes:
- avoid annotating default serviceaccount; don't break any infra pods.
- make sure any Role/RoleBinding in analytics namespace grants required permissions to the SA. Example RoleBinding: ```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: analytics-reader-binding
  namespace: analytics
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: analytics-sa
  namespace: analytics
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: analytics-read-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

sre-anna: also FYI if pods use projected tokens directly you can control audience/expiration via the TokenRequest in code; the SA annotation only maps an IAM role.

tom_s: one more: if this is in a kustomize overlay please add the change there too so future syncs don't revert.

maria_garcia: thanks all — will run apply during the maintenance window and ping here after. I'll also add the RoleBinding and update kustomize overlay. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: apply queued (maintenance-window: 2025-06-02T02:00:00Z).
